author: rungodrungo
text: @piphop As I understand it a FL is a decision point that confines a larger flag/range/rectangle. Depending on the time frame, the larger flag represents accumulation or distribution by larger entities (or just fluctuation in a range on HTFs), which by its very nature means a pause in the "trend," so the momentum of a larger movement is, at that point, considered lost (as you saw, price changed direction, though it is common for momentum to pick up in the same direction again) Also, I understand that what distinguishes a RBR/DBR/etc. from a FL is price's tendency to form a flag adjacent to that level so the term FL cant really be used until a FTB. Flags happen when price pulls over on the side of the road to look at its map. p=m*v where v=0, if you will As always, if I'm wrong, someone please correct me for pophop's sake.
